operation: Reviewed exact OOXML prose/ethics edits; preserve pre-existing paragraphs, tables, formulas, styles and media

changes.before: Short calibration runs force longitudinal EEG decoders to learn from few new labels. We quantified the value of updating the spatial representation after accounting for classifier recalibration and examined the prediction changes producing that value. Using Kumar2024, we compared frozen common spatial patterns and linear discriminant analysis (CSP/LDA), LDA-only recalibration, and full CSP/LDA refitting across 18 participants and six sessions. Both updating methods used the same 40 source labels and 19 or 20 current-session labels. Six predefined participants formed the development group and 12 the primary cohort. In the primary cohort, full refitting achieved 65.36% balanced accuracy, exceeding frozen decoding by 7.42 percentage points (95% participant-bootstrap interval 2.49–12.48) and LDA-only recalibration by 5.47 points (2.17–8.91). The latter accounted for 73.7% of the mean total gain. An additional prediction-transition analysis resolved this component gain into 16.04 points of corrected errors and 10.57 points of newly introduced errors. Mean left- and right-class recall increased by 6.16 and 4.78 points, respectively. The component gain was positive in ten of 12 participant averages, in each of the five target-session cohort averages, and across all single-participant deletion summaries. Development measurements distinguished calibration-subset agreement from correct task-score orientation: nine of 30 support sessions had opposite orientations between halves. Chronological evaluation, participant-level inference, amplitude sensitivity and complete neural-reference histories supported the comparisons. Spatial-filter refitting therefore contributed most of the observed recalibration gain under matched labels, with mean recall improvements in both classes. The findings identify update location and calibration-measurement direction as concrete targets for efficient longitudinal EEG recalibration.

changes.before: Participants sub-1, 4, 7, 10, 13 and 16 formed the development group. The remaining 12 formed the predefined primary cohort, allocated by numeric identifier before examination of these results. In session 0, runs 0 and 1 supplied 40 source training windows, run 2 supplied 20 source-validation windows, and run 3 supplied source query. In each of five later sessions, run 0 supplied support and the remaining whole runs supplied query.
changes.after: Participants sub-1, 4, 7, 10, 13 and 16, selected at every third numeric identifier, formed the predefined development group for calibration-reliability probes and pipeline verification. The remaining 12 formed the predefined primary cohort. Both cohorts used the same fixed four-component CSP, Ledoit–Wolf regularization and automatic-shrinkage LDA configuration; the primary-cohort results were not used to tune these settings. In session 0, runs 0 and 1 supplied 40 source training windows, run 2 supplied 20 source-validation windows, and run 3 supplied source query. In each of five later sessions, run 0 supplied support and the remaining whole runs supplied query.

changes.before: The two CPU update methods share the adaptation budget. Their comparison with freezing measures the benefit of adding support labels and refitting the specified components. EEGNet supplies a source-only neural reference with the additional validation budget shown in Table 1. S1 Text, S3 gives the complete implementation settings.
changes.after: The two CPU update methods share the adaptation budget. Their comparison with freezing measures the benefit of adding support labels and refitting the specified components. Frozen EEGNet supplies a source-only neural reference with the additional validation budget shown in Table 1. Target-session neural fine-tuning would add layer-freezing and learning-rate choices for 19 or 20 support trials; retaining the frozen reference keeps the adaptation comparison focused on the CSP and LDA stages. S1 Text, S3 gives the complete implementation settings.

changes.before: The original endpoint hierarchy and cohort allocation preceded the reported results. Later QC, influence and post-review statistical checks were exploratory after inspection of those results. The latter checks enumerated all  sign assignments for four saved participant-level contrasts: full minus frozen, full minus LDA-only, and LDA-only minus frozen in the primary cohort, plus full minus frozen in the ten-person unflagged sensitivity. The statistic was the absolute mean paired difference, with a  tolerance in BA units at the tail boundary. This reference construction assumes independent participant differences with sign symmetry about zero. We report unadjusted values and Holm adjustment across the four checks. S1 Text, S11 specifies the enumeration and its relationship to the original bootstrap intervals.
changes.after: The original endpoint hierarchy and cohort allocation preceded the reported results. changes.before: We assessed two measures of session change relative to source query. The task-axis measure used the source-trained, normalized difference between class means in standardized 44-dimensional mu/beta log-power coordinates; one-dimensional Wasserstein distance measured change along this axis. The covariance-shape measure used a source-training Riemannian reference in a fixed 21-dimensional common-average-reference basis, with trace normalization and fixed shrinkage. It captures normalized covariance shape. Target labels entered the BA outcome, while the drift predictors used the corresponding signal distributions.
changes.after: We assessed whether signal-distribution changes tracked changes in frozen-decoder BA. The task-axis measure was the one-dimensional Wasserstein distance between source-query and target-query projections onto the source-trained, normalized right-minus-left class direction in standardized 44-dimensional mu/beta log-power coordinates (8–13 and 13–30 Hz). For covariance-shape drift, each epoch’s covariance matrix was trace-normalized and shrinkage-regularized in a fixed 21-dimensional common-average-reference basis. We subtracted the source-query mean Riemannian distance to the source-training reference from the target-query mean distance to that same reference. Both predictors used target signals without target labels; labels entered the BA outcome.

changes.before: The outcome was target-minus-source frozen-decoder BA. Associations pooled within- and between-participant variation and shared a source-query reference across each participant’s five target sessions. The participant-block bootstrap preserved that clustering. These query-distribution associations served as retrospective descriptions.
changes.after: The outcome was target-minus-source frozen-decoder BA across the primary cohort’s 60 target sessions. Spearman associations pooled within- and between-participant variation and shared a source-query reference across each participant’s five target sessions. We used 2,000 participant-block bootstrap resamples to preserve that clustering. These query-distribution associations were descriptive analyses, separate from update-policy selection.

changes.before: Development-only reliability probes used source training and current support. Fixed power, PCA and supervised CSP-score measurements were evaluated using source-run grouping, chronological support halves and cyclic-label controls. Each source-run probe trained on one 20-event run and evaluated the other, then reversed the roles. All learned transformations, including CSP and LDA, were fitted within the training fold.
changes.after: Development-only reliability probes used source training and current support to examine the task information available from short calibration runs. Three low-dimensional probes used standardized 44-dimensional mu/beta log power, four source-fitted principal components, or six C3/Cz/C4 mu/beta coordinates, each classified using the right-minus-left class-centroid axis and midpoint threshold. A fourth probe used supervised four-component CSP/LDA. Each source-run probe trained on one 20-event run and evaluated the other, then reversed the roles. Standardization, PCA, CSP and LDA were fitted within the training fold as applicable.

changes.before: Support measurements used the source models fitted on 40 training events, with source-fitted coordinate scales. Each class was divided into chronological halves within the support run. Vector cosines and signed source-score contrasts measured agreement and class orientation. Cyclic controls enumerated prescribed label phases within run grouping and were interpreted as alignment sensitivities. All 240 supervised fold/rotation pipelines were retained. S1 Text, S4–S6 specifies half sizes, score orientation, controls and degenerate cases.
changes.after: For the supervised cyclic-label controls, each of six participants contributed two source-run folds and 20 training-label rotations, giving 6 × 2 × 20 = 240 fitted CSP/LDA pipelines. Held-out label rotations entered scoring only, yielding all 20 × 20 joint label-phase pairs per participant. These controls measured sensitivity to label alignment.

changes.before: In the primary cohort, the Spearman associations of covariance-shape change and source-task-axis Wasserstein distance with frozen BA change were −0.007 (−0.505–0.438) and 0.197 (−0.240–0.518), respectively. These measures summarize the relation between signal-distribution change and frozen-decoder performance.
changes.after: In the primary cohort, covariance-shape drift and task-axis Wasserstein distance had Spearman associations of −0.007 (95% interval −0.505 to 0.438) and 0.197 (−0.240 to 0.518) with target-minus-source frozen BA change. These estimates did not establish a reliable relationship between either fixed drift summary and frozen-decoder performance loss.

changes.before: Development power, PCA and motor-band probes achieved mean source BA of 51.67%, 50.00% and 54.17%, with intervals including 50%. Supervised CSP/LDA source-run probes achieved 62.9167% (52.5–71.6667). The participant-averaged support-vector cosine was 0.295325 (0.032041–0.573003). Signed scores separated two properties of short-run calibration: agreement between subsets and class orientation relative to the source decoder. Among 30 support sessions, both half-contrasts were positive in 19, both were negative in two, and the signs differed in nine (Fig 3). Five support sessions had single-class source-score predictions. The two double-negative sessions demonstrate that agreement can coexist with reversed class orientation; the nine opposite-sign sessions identify changes in the sampled direction. Both quantities are needed to characterize the task information available from a short support run.
changes.after: The development source-run probes using standardized power, PCA and C3/Cz/C4 motor-band coordinates achieved mean BA of 51.67%, 50.00% and 54.17%, respectively, with all 95% intervals including 50%. Supervised CSP/LDA achieved 62.92% (52.50–71.67). The participant-averaged cosine between support-half vectors in the source-standardized CSP space was 0.295 (0.032–0.573). Among 30 support sessions, both signed LDA half-margins were positive in 19, both were negative in two, and the signs differed in nine (Fig 3). Five support sessions had single-class source-score predictions. The double-negative sessions show that agreement can coexist with reversed class orientation; the opposite-sign sessions show that the estimated orientation can change within a 19- or 20-trial support run. Subset agreement and class orientation therefore describe distinct aspects of calibration reliability.

changes.before: All sign assignments were enumerated using the stated numerical tolerance. The unflagged ten-person contrast had a positive percentile-bootstrap interval and an unadjusted sign-flip p value of 0.07617; the interval and test use different reference constructions. These exploratory checks complement the effect estimates and their uncertainty.
changes.after: All 2^(n) sign assignments were enumerated using the stated numerical tolerance. The percentile-bootstrap intervals summarize paired participant resampling, whereas the exact tests use a sign-symmetric null distribution and Holm adjustment addresses the four-contrast family, including the overlapping 12- and ten-participant sets. These distinct reference constructions explain why an interval excluding zero need not correspond to a Holm-adjusted p value below 0.05. For the unflagged ten-person contrast, the 95% bootstrap interval was 0.99–11.24 points and the unadjusted sign-flip p value was 0.07617.

changes.before: The development group, participant differences and session trajectories remain informative for choosing future updates. The mean component contrast was −1.15 points in development and +5.47 in the primary cohort; individual target-session gains also changed direction. These data support treating the expected benefit of an action as a distinct quantity to estimate. A useful selection target is the gain from an LDA-only or full update relative to the available alternatives, with current source/support information supplying the decision inputs.
changes.after: Across all 18 participants, the secondary summary favored full refitting over LDA-only by 3.26 points and over freezing by 6.03 points. The component contrast was −1.15 points in development and +5.47 in the primary cohort. Session-level differences included a 37.50-point full-minus-LDA-only decrease for development participant sub-7 in session 2. Thus, the positive overall result coexisted with marked variation in which update performed best.

changes.before: The present evidence comes from cue-anchored offline decoding in one 18-participant dataset, with the added decompositions and sensitivity checks treated as exploratory; phase-specific signals, independent cohorts and prospective update selection define the next validation targets, while the neural reference is tied to its recorded source-only budget.
changes.after: Four features define the scope and next tests. First, the five-second cue-anchored windows include the approximately 1.5-second visual cue and subsequent task activity; variable online trial endings can also place feedback or post-task activity within a complete window. Strictly task-anchored windows would address a different phase-specific endpoint. The amplitude rule flagged 1,512 of 7,156 windows (21.1%) and the query sensitivity retained positive mean gains; this check addresses large query amplitudes, while potential artifacts in training/support data remain a separate issue.

The secondary all-18 summary favored full refitting by 3.26 points over LDA-only and 6.03 over freezing. Development measurements distinguished calibration-subset agreement from correct task-score orientation: nine of 30 support sessions had opposite orientations between halves. Chronological evaluation, participant-level inference, amplitude sensitivity and complete neural-reference histories supported the comparisons. Spatial-filter refitting therefore contributed most of the observed recalibration gain under matched labels, with mean recall improvements in both classes. The findings identify update location and calibration-measurement direction as concrete targets for efficient longitudinal EEG recalibration.

changes.before: We assessed two measures of session change relative to source query. The task-axis measure used the source-trained, normalized difference between class means in standardized 44-dimensional mu/beta log-power coordinates; one-dimensional Wasserstein distance measured change along this axis. The covariance-shape measure used a source-training Riemannian reference in a fixed 21-dimensional common-average-reference basis, with trace normalization and fixed shrinkage. It captures normalized covariance shape. Target labels entered the BA outcome, while the drift predictors used the corresponding signal distributions.
changes.after: We assessed whether signal-distribution changes tracked changes in frozen-decoder BA. The task-axis measure was the one-dimensional Wasserstein distance between source-query and target-query projections onto the source-trained, normalized right-minus-left class direction in standardized 44-dimensional mu/beta log-power coordinates (8–13 and 13–30 Hz). For covariance-shape drift, each epoch’s covariance matrix was trace-normalized and shrinkage-regularized in a fixed 21-dimensional common-average-reference basis. We subtracted the source-query mean Riemannian distance to the source-training reference from the target-query mean distance to that same reference. Both predictors used target signals without target labels; labels entered the BA outcome.

changes.before: The outcome was target-minus-source frozen-decoder BA. Associations pooled within- and between-participant variation and shared a source-query reference across each participant’s five target sessions. The participant-block bootstrap preserved that clustering. These query-distribution associations served as retrospective descriptions.
changes.after: The outcome was target-minus-source frozen-decoder BA across the primary cohort’s 60 target sessions. Spearman associations pooled within- and between-participant variation and shared a source-query reference across each participant’s five target sessions. We used 2,000 participant-block bootstrap resamples to preserve that clustering. These query-distribution associations were descriptive analyses, separate from update-policy selection.

changes.before: Development-only reliability probes used source training and current support. Fixed power, PCA and supervised CSP-score measurements were evaluated using source-run grouping, chronological support halves and cyclic-label controls. Each source-run probe trained on one 20-event run and evaluated the other, then reversed the roles. All learned transformations, including CSP and LDA, were fitted within the training fold.
changes.after: Development-only reliability probes used source training and current support to examine the task information available from short calibration runs. Three low-dimensional probes used standardized 44-dimensional mu/beta log power, four source-fitted principal components, or six C3/Cz/C4 mu/beta coordinates, each classified using the right-minus-left class-centroid axis and midpoint threshold. A fourth probe used supervised four-component CSP/LDA. Each source-run probe trained on one 20-event run and evaluated the other, then reversed the roles. Standardization, PCA, CSP and LDA were fitted within the training fold as applicable.

changes.before: Support measurements used the source models fitted on 40 training events, with source-fitted coordinate scales. Each class was divided into chronological halves within the support run. Vector cosines and signed source-score contrasts measured agreement and class orientation. Cyclic controls enumerated prescribed label phases within run grouping and were interpreted as alignment sensitivities. All 240 supervised fold/rotation pipelines were retained. S1 Text, S4–S6 specifies half sizes, score orientation, controls and degenerate cases.
changes.after: For the supervised cyclic-label controls, each of six participants contributed two source-run folds and 20 training-label rotations, giving 6 × 2 × 20 = 240 fitted CSP/LDA pipelines. Held-out label rotations entered scoring only, yielding all 20 × 20 joint label-phase pairs per participant. These controls measured sensitivity to label alignment.

changes.before: In the primary cohort, the Spearman associations of covariance-shape change and source-task-axis Wasserstein distance with frozen BA change were −0.007 (−0.505–0.438) and 0.197 (−0.240–0.518), respectively. These measures summarize the relation between signal-distribution change and frozen-decoder performance.
changes.after: In the primary cohort, covariance-shape drift and task-axis Wasserstein distance had Spearman associations of −0.007 (95% interval −0.505 to 0.438) and 0.197 (−0.240 to 0.518) with target-minus-source frozen BA change. These estimates did not establish a reliable relationship between either fixed drift summary and frozen-decoder performance loss.

changes.before: Development power, PCA and motor-band probes achieved mean source BA of 51.67%, 50.00% and 54.17%, with intervals including 50%. Supervised CSP/LDA source-run probes achieved 62.9167% (52.5–71.6667). The participant-averaged support-vector cosine was 0.295325 (0.032041–0.573003). Signed scores separated two properties of short-run calibration: agreement between subsets and class orientation relative to the source decoder. Among 30 support sessions, both half-contrasts were positive in 19, both were negative in two, and the signs differed in nine (Fig 3). Five support sessions had single-class source-score predictions. The two double-negative sessions demonstrate that agreement can coexist with reversed class orientation; the nine opposite-sign sessions identify changes in the sampled direction. Both quantities are needed to characterize the task information available from a short support run.
changes.after: The development source-run probes using standardized power, PCA and C3/Cz/C4 motor-band coordinates achieved mean BA of 51.67%, 50.00% and 54.17%, respectively, with all 95% intervals including 50%. Supervised CSP/LDA achieved 62.92% (52.50–71.67). The participant-averaged cosine between support-half vectors in the source-standardized CSP space was 0.295 (0.032–0.573). Among 30 support sessions, both signed LDA half-margins were positive in 19, both were negative in two, and the signs differed in nine (Fig 3). Five support sessions had single-class source-score predictions. The double-negative sessions show that agreement can coexist with reversed class orientation; the opposite-sign sessions show that the estimated orientation can change within a 19- or 20-trial support run. Subset agreement and class orientation therefore describe distinct aspects of calibration reliability.

changes.after: All 2^(n) sign assignments were enumerated using the stated numerical tolerance. The percentile-bootstrap intervals summarize paired participant resampling, whereas the exact tests use a sign-symmetric null distribution and Holm adjustment addresses the four-contrast family, including the overlapping 12- and ten-participant sets. These distinct reference constructions explain why an interval excluding zero need not correspond to a Holm-adjusted p value below 0.05. For the unflagged ten-person contrast, the 95% bootstrap interval was 0.99–11.24 points and the unadjusted sign-flip p value was 0.07617.

changes.before: The development group, participant differences and session trajectories remain informative for choosing future updates. The mean component contrast was −1.15 points in development and +5.47 in the primary cohort; individual target-session gains also changed direction. These data support treating the expected benefit of an action as a distinct quantity to estimate. A useful selection target is the gain from an LDA-only or full update relative to the available alternatives, with current source/support information supplying the decision inputs.
changes.after: Across all 18 participants, the secondary summary favored full refitting over LDA-only by 3.26 points and over freezing by 6.03 points. The component contrast was −1.15 points in development and +5.47 in the primary cohort. Session-level differences included a 37.50-point full-minus-LDA-only decrease for development participant sub-7 in session 2. Thus, the positive overall result coexisted with marked variation in which update performed best.

changes.before: The present evidence comes from cue-anchored offline decoding in one 18-participant dataset, with the added decompositions and sensitivity checks treated as exploratory; phase-specific signals, independent cohorts and prospective update selection define the next validation targets, while the neural reference is tied to its recorded source-only budget.
changes.after: Four features define the scope and next tests.
